title: A core has no row of its own to tick in Deactivate parts
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-COREALONE-01), with description {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL COREALONE PART), is tracked at {Location-A} with a Core Charge (for example $25.00), so it has a core, {Core-A}, described "Core for {Description-A}".
  • {Part-A} and {Core-A} are active.
custom_steps:
1. On the Active tab open the ⋮ actions menu and click "Deactivate parts".
  2. Search "Core for {Description-A}".
  3. Clear the search and search {Part-A}.
  4. Click × on the bulk bar.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: No row is listed for {Core-A}: the core has no row of its own, so there is nothing to tick for it.
  • Step 3: Exactly one row is listed, {Part-A}'s own, with its core charge in the "Core" column. No separate row for {Core-A} appears.
  • Step 4: The mode ends and nothing has changed: {Part-A} is still on the Active tab. The core's own refusal, "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead.", cannot be reached on screen because the core cannot be ticked: write 'not checked by hand' for it in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S5-E3, S2-N3, S10-R13a, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas 13 Oct copy: no board shows a core. Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 6): a core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
  • S2-N3: “A core cannot be set active or inactive on its own. Asked to, the system refuses it with "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead."”
  • S10-R13a: “The reasons are "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead.", "Part not found." and "Part is already in that state."”
  • PRD §8 User Feedback Summary (A core asked to change status on its own): “"A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead." | Listed as the failure reason”
